title: Automate org access controls and compliance evidence for residency & retention
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood must provide provable controls around who can access customer data and where evidence of that access (audit logs and retention proof) is stored. This ticket consolidates work to: 1) standardize RBAC roles and enforcement across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments; 2) complete SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning integration for org-level user lifecycle; 3) automate periodic access reviews and generate signed evidence bundles that respect data residency and retention policies.

Goals:
- Define canonical RBAC model and role-to-permission mapping used by Console and Private control plane.
- Ensure SSO (SAML) flows are instrumented to create audit entries tied to residency metadata (region, tenant control plane).
- Implement two-way SCIM provisioning with state reconciliation and soft-delete retention windows.
- Build evidence export pipeline that generates time-bounded, signed compliance reports (role assignments, SSO login events, SCIM events, and admin actions) stored in region-specific S3/GCS buckets with retention TTL.
- Automate periodic access review reminders and capture attestations in the evidence store.

Acceptance criteria:
- RBAC policy spec merged and consumed by runtime (policy schema v1).
- SAML login events include residency tags and are routed to per-region audit store within 30s of event generation.
- SCIM sync completes reconciliation end-to-end for a test org with 10k users; provisioning latency < 60s for create/update flows.
- Evidence export tool (CLI + scheduled job) can produce a signed ZIP containing role snapshot, login events, and provisioning deltas for any date range and region; export validated by compliance team.
- Automated reminders created and tracked; 95% of reviewers complete attestation in less than 7 days in pilot.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- RBAC: prefer coarse-grained role sets by default (Admin/Dev/Observer/Support) with optional custom roles. Coarse roles reduce audit noise; custom roles require deterministic diffs for evidence exports.
- Residency tagging: attach region and control-plane-id at event emit time instead of post-processing to avoid cross-region joins and to simplify retention policy enforcement.
- Evidence storage: use per-region buckets to satisfy legal residency. Keep objects small (ndjson) and sign manifests with KMS per-region. KMS integration will require separate key policies for Dedicated/private customers.
- SCIM: support incremental syncs using change tokens; for on-prem/private deployments where outbound webhooks are restricted, provide pull-mode via secure agent.
- Periodic reviews: store attestations as signed artifacts tied to reviewer identity via SSO assertion to minimize repudiation risk.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) RBAC schema PR and runtime adaptor (ENG runtime + Console RBAC enforcement) - owners: runtime/security team.
2) SAML instrumentation RFC and small SDK for residency tagging - owners: auth-platform.
3) SCIM connector enhancements and agent for private deployments - owners: provisioning team.
4) Evidence pipeline: event collector -> per-region staging -> signer (KMS) -> export generator + retention TTL enforcement - owners: observability & infra.
5) Access review automation: Console UI for reviewers, scheduled worker to generate reminders, and attestation storage - owners: console/frontend + backend.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase 1 (pilot): internal Redwood org + two pilot customers (one hosted, one dedicated) to validate SAML tagging, SCIM reconciliation, and evidence exports.
- Phase 2: opt-in beta for all customers with Console flags to enable attestations and automated exports.
- Phase 3: GA with documented APIs and Managed Private agent (for on-prem) and SLA considerations for retention + cross-region exports.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Audit event delivery: 99.9% within 60s.
- SCIM reconciliation success: 99.5% for provisioned attributes.
- Evidence export generation: 95% of requests complete within 2 minutes for 30-day windows.
- Alerting: failed sign operations, KMS permission errors, cross-region retention policy violations.

Fallbacks and rollback:
- If signer KMS in a region is misconfigured, route to a quarantined bucket and trigger manual compliance workflow; do not drop events.
- For breaking RBAC changes, support runtime feature flag to revert to previous role mapping for affected orgs.

Open questions / next steps:
- Need legal input on minimum artifact retention for signed attestations (ask Legal for policy).
- Decide retention TTL defaults by region and make them configurable per org.
- Confirm whether Dedicated customers require separate signing keys or can share multi-tenant keys with strict IAM constraints.

Links to design artifacts and tracking:
- Confluence: https://confluence.internal.redwood/org-access-governance (draft spec)
- RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/718
- Prototype SCIM agent: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scim-agent/tree/feature/pilot

Notes:
This ticket is intentionally cross-functional and will require 2-3 paired sessions between runtime, auth-platform, and observability teams in the next cycle to unblock integration points.
